evidence.reason: The current code still checks only that the interrupted recover exited nonzero (`rc not in (0, None)`), which cannot distinguish a SIGKILL (-9) from an ordinary refusal. A normal refusal that leaves the pending `drained` record unchanged would satisfy both this predicate and the later record assertions, so the test can falsely report an interrupted recovery even if the `drain` kill hook never fired. Requiring the exact SIGKILL status is the smallest compatible correctness fix for the interruption test; the same predicate remains at current line 1342.
